blockers: The pinned upstream repository tree contains README.md, README.zh-CN.md, LICENSE and media assets, but no scripts/simulation or scripts/metrics paths although the README describes those paths in its project-layout section.
A runnable and revision-pinned official evaluation implementation has not been located in the pinned repository tree; no substitute runner is silently inferred.
No file-level SHA-256 inventory for the rigid-body physical measurement payloads has been captured.

Only representative bouncing-ball and Newton's-cradle trial JSON files have been structurally inspected; all eight rigid task families, material branches and trial files still require a complete schema audit.
Per-sample measurement uncertainty/covariance, calibration uncertainty propagation, missing-frame policy, outlier policy and recording-level grouping have not yet been fully audited.
The MIT license is a Hub metadata declaration; its application to every data artifact, embedded asset and external dependency has not been independently reviewed.
No use/mirroring approval decision has been made for the exact physical-trial payloads.

The paper states 180 Hz camera acquisition followed by truncation to the valid experiment interval and downsampling to 30 FPS for released trajectory JSON. The exact resampling/filter method, sample phase, timestamp reconstruction and uncertainty propagation through downsampling are not identified in the inspected artifacts.

The 30 FPS exported trajectories cannot by themselves establish peak contact force or sub-frame impact timing. The task-specific GAUGE momentum-transfer metric is not a direct contact-force measurement; impact/impulse claims require a separate observability and measurement qualification.

GAUGE paper (arXiv:2608.05948, 2026-08-06) states that 16 NOKOV Mars9H cameras acquire at 180 Hz with sub-millimetre localization; each recording is truncated to the valid interval then downsampled to 30 FPS for JSON. Rigid/textile simulator states are also recorded at 30 Hz after 180 Hz simulation; deformable simulation runs at 900 Hz but states are recorded at 30 Hz.
